headline: Start day is here. The taper held and the engine is banked. From tomorrow the 580 km trail becomes the only data that matters.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: Everything about the recent picture reads as a clean pre-event hold rather than a training block. The last week of running has been deliberately short and easy — controlled efforts sitting low in the aerobic range, nothing reaching into the harder territory the engine is clearly capable of. That's exactly what you'd want going into a multi-day self-supported crossing: legs unloaded, no residual fatigue banked from a hard session. Strength stayed live right to the edge without accumulating cost, which matches how you've handled the final quiet window. Steps remain very high, driven by the background movement and logistics travel rather than tracked training — so the low run volume badly understates actual time on feet. Recovery figures and the strain reading look suppressed, but that's the taper by design, not a warning; the detraining label is an artefact of dialled-back tracked load, not a real loss of the base you've built all year.
sections.trends: The year-to-date shape is unambiguous — you're sitting at nearly four times the distance you'd logged by this date last year, and the recent four weeks stepped up meaningfully over the prior block before the taper flattened the last few days. That's a genuine build followed by a purposeful drawdown, not a plateau or a stall. The arc makes complete sense given what starts tomorrow: you spent the summer accumulating durable base and back-to-back capacity, then pulled the plug on volume at precisely the right moment. Nothing in the trend contradicts readiness for a long, cumulative effort.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace has held flat at its early-July mark, which is appropriate — you haven't done the kind of sustained hard work that moves this number in weeks, nor should you have going into a taper. The single genuinely hard session in the recent window, that long tempo-heavy run in late July, confirms the top end is intact and available. For the crossing itself this figure is largely academic; what matters is that the aerobic ceiling is sound and untouched by fatigue. It'll sit here until trail rhythm resets what "steady" feels like.
sections.zones: The recent per-session shapes are exactly right for the moment: the last several runs sit almost entirely in the lowest two zones, with only brief touches higher, and the harder long run three weeks back is the clear outlier that proved the engine before you backed off. There's no grey-zone creep in the taper runs — they're honestly easy, not accidentally moderate. That discipline is what leaves the legs genuinely fresh rather than lightly-cooked. The distribution matches the intent of the window perfectly; the real test is how this zone map redraws itself under a loaded pack.
sections.hr_comparison: Strength sessions have run without chest-strap HR recently, so there's no fresh per-session shape to read there, but the earlier strength data sat comfortably low — these are functional sessions, not cardiovascular hammering, which is exactly why they didn't interfere with the taper. Where run HR is available, avg and max track sensibly against pace with no odd disagreement worth flagging. Nothing anomalous in the sensor picture.
sections.calendar: The frequency pattern shows the run streak intact at its all-time best and strength holding its own multi-week run, right up to the final days before the start — you didn't let consistency lapse just because volume dropped. That's the meaningful signal: the taper was a load reduction, not a training pause. Frequency stayed high while intensity and distance came down, which is the cleaner way to arrive fresh without going stale.
sections.personal_bests: None of the road PBs are in play here — the crossing is a different discipline entirely, and your speed bests date from last autumn's sharper block. What's relevant instead is your longest-effort and 50K durability marks: the next ten days will push well beyond anything in that history in cumulative terms, so the real "best" on the table is a multi-day time-on-feet record rather than any pace figure.

watch_items: Watch how easy-day HR recalibrates once the pack and consecutive loaded days stack — the first few days will reset your sense of what steady costs.
Track the back-to-back leg response early; cumulative durability under load, not the engine, is the genuine unknown.
Read the border mountain crossing as its own terrain spike, distinct from the flatter coastal sections.
Watch whether nightly recovery settles once trail rhythm replaces the travel-and-logistics window.
